title: Linux Matters homepage: fixed nav, banner, subscribe badges, episode grid
stressor: a real-world Bootstrap-grid podcast homepage with a fixed nav, banner, subscribe-badge row, multi-column episode card grid, and pagination - real page structure that scrolls, used to catch overlay scroll-dance regressions across snapshot generations
attribution: Markup and copy frozen from the live Linux Matters homepage on 2026-07-04 for offline corpus use. Provenance only: Linux Matters is the maintainer's own project.
notes: Self-contained single page, all CSS inline, no script, no network URLs. Frozen from https://linuxmatters.sh/ on 2026-07-04. Bootstrap 4.6.2, Font Awesome, mediaelement, and Google Fonts Poppins are not loaded; the kept Bootstrap grid classes are re-styled with plain inline CSS at the md breakpoint for a 960px viewport, and Poppins falls back to a generic sans-serif. Structure: a fixed-top nav bar, an episode banner with a number overlay, a Show Summary block, a jumbotron with intro copy plus three round host avatars and a subscribe-badge row, a three-column Past Episodes card grid, a pagination row, and a footer. All images are placeholder solid-fill data URIs at the real display dimensions; geometry matters, pixels do not. Designed to be tall enough to scroll for the scroll-dance leg. Placement gates cleanly on the current build at all three geometries: 120x40 mean 0.240 max 0.500; 240x48 and the real-geometry 158x86 leg (cell 16x33, layout_scale 1.975) mean about 0.26 max 0.500; drifted 0, collisions 0, offgrid 0 everywhere. The scroll-dance leg is a hard gate at danced 0. The scroll-dance metric classifies the position:fixed nav (13 runs that stay at the viewport top on scroll) as fixed and scores every other run on its own scroll-compensated document row round((Y+scrollY)/cellH), so a fixed nav and scrolling body content each read honestly rather than the fixed nav counting against the body's median shift. The compose-time scroll shift re-snaps each run's cell from the shifted box origin the same way mapBoxToCells decodes, so a mid-scroll frame and the settle re-decode land the same row and no body run hops one cell when the scroll settles. Together these score danced 0, re-placements 0 of 65 matched runs (13 fixed, 52 glued) at 158x86 cell 16x33 capture=3 scroll=600, with no runs dropped. The shift also reads the viewport-anchored boxes the walk reports beside the runs, so it holds a run inside the fixed nav in place instead of translating it, and drops a body run that the shift moves under the nav's opaque background. That is what makes the mid-scroll frame agree with the settled one on this page: before it, the pre-settle frame classified 0 runs as fixed, because the shift had slid the nav's own text off the nav.

scroll_dance_gate.reason: Hard-gate thresholds, met on the current build: danced 0, re-placements 0 of 65 matched runs (13 fixed nav, 52 glued body) at 158x86 cell 16x33 capture=3 scroll=600. The metric classifies the position:fixed nav as viewport-stationary rather than counting it against the body's scroll, and the compose shift re-snaps from the shifted box origin so no body run hops a row at settle. Keep danced 0 and replacements 0 as the regression guard. The approved run counts alongside this gate were re-measured when the shift learned the walk's viewport-anchored boxes: pre-settle 56 matched runs, 13 fixed and 43 body, against 46 matched runs, 0 fixed and 46 body before it, with the settled leg unchanged at 61 matched, 13 fixed and 48 body. Both legs are stable across repeated runs.
